summary: Almost everyone entering Tuvalu gets a visa on arrival at Funafuti for up to one month — free for citizens of the countries listed in its Immigration Regulations, among them the UK, Fiji and Samoa, AUD 100 for others — while EU passport holders (except Irish) are visa-exempt for 90 days in any 180 under the EU–Tuvalu agreement.

fee.notes: Set by the Immigration Regulations 2014 (regulation 2). Citizens of the countries listed in Schedule 1 — among them the UK, Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Tonga, Vanuatu, Malaysia and South Korea — pay nothing, and the Minister may waive the fee for others. Carry Australian dollars in cash, as cards cannot be used at the airport.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for entry to Tuvalu. Canada's travel advice tells travellers to get insurance that covers medical evacuation and hospital stays.

onwardTicket.text: A confirmed onward or return ticket is required for the visa on arrival.

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors must show sufficient funds and a confirmed place to stay.

declarations.text: Every passenger arriving by air or sea, except commercial crew, must complete a paper arrival card (Form 11 of the Immigration Regulations 2014), and a departure card on leaving.

source.name: Government of Tuvalu — Immigration Regulations 2014, arrival cards
source.instrument: Immigration Regulations 2014, regulation 9 and Schedule 2 Form 11 (made under section 5(2) of the Immigration Act)

currencyLimits.text: No official source we could read states whether, or above what amount, cash must be declared when entering or leaving Tuvalu. The UK Foreign Office says you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

source.name: UK FCDO — Tuvalu travel advice (entry requirements)

notes: Tuvalu uses the Australian dollar. The UK and Canada say there are no ATMs and that card payments are not accepted, so bring enough cash.
The UK says it is illegal to import, export, cultivate or distribute drugs in Tuvalu, with penalties that include fines and imprisonment.

payments.text: The UK and Canada both say there are no ATMs in Tuvalu and that credit and debit card payments are not accepted. Bring enough Australian dollars in cash for your whole stay.

safety.text: Canada's travel advice says the crime rate is very low, though petty crime occurs. The UK government's travel advice says Tuvalu's only hospital is on Funafuti and is adequate for routine treatment, that serious cases may need medical evacuation to Fiji or Australia, and that the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May, though cyclones can happen at any time of year.

tips.text: There are no ATMs in Tuvalu and card payments are not accepted, according to the UK and Canada. Arrive with enough Australian dollars in cash for your visa, accommodation and food.
The UK advises drinking or using only boiled or bottled water and avoiding ice in drinks. Canada says shortages of fresh water occur and that bottled water may be in short supply.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tuvalu?
faq.answer: Practically everyone can get one on arrival at Funafuti for a stay of up to one month, so no advance application is normally needed. Citizens of the countries listed in Schedule 1 of the Immigration Regulations 2014 — including the UK, Malaysia, South Korea, Fiji, Kenya and several Caribbean states — pay nothing, other nationalities pay AUD 100 unless the Minister waives it, EU passport holders (except Irish) are visa-exempt for 90 days in any 180 under the EU–Tuvalu agreement.

faq.question: How much does the Tuvalu visa on arrival cost?
faq.answer: AUD 100, set by the Immigration Regulations 2014, unless you are a citizen of one of the countries listed in Schedule 1 — among them the UK, Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Tonga, Malaysia and South Korea — who pay nothing; the Minister may also waive it. There are no card facilities at the airport, so bring the fee in Australian dollars in cash.

faq.question: Can I stay longer than a month?
faq.answer: Yes, in principle. Apply to the Immigration Department on Funafuti before your permitted stay expires; extensions are granted at their discretion, typically month by month, and you will need your passport, onward ticket and proof of funds.

faq.question: Are there ATMs or card payments in Tuvalu?
faq.answer: No. The UK and Canada both say there are no ATMs in Tuvalu and that credit and debit card payments are not accepted. Bring all the Australian dollars you need for the trip.
